Action items assigned and a follow-up council scheduled.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 08:45 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Samira, Elliot, Noah, Grace, Marcus, Rina
Shared links: https://drive.redwood/winter-deck-v3.pdf; https://confluence.redwood/ops/runbook-draft; slack: #leadership-brief

[00:00] Maya: Okay, let's get started. Um, thanks everyone for carving out time this morning. I know it's a busy week. Quick agenda run — hiring ask, product tradeoffs, private deployments pipeline, ops and incident playbook, and pulse. Anything to add?

[00:23] Liam: No, that's good. I'll flag a small infra note on capacity for demo environments later in the deck.

[00:35] Samira: And I'll cover a couple of customer asks that are pushing us to revisit some latency SLAs.

[00:42] Maya: Cool. Marcus you want to... no, you're just listening for sales signals — fine. Alright, Samira take us through the product bits.

[00:50] Samira: Great. Slide 6 in the deck — so we've been getting repeated asks from mid-market customers for sub-80ms median token latency on short-form generation. Our hosted offering can hit that with XLA kernels for certain model variants, and Dedicated can, but at a pretty sharp cost delta. I'm showing two scenarios: keep current default (balanced) or push a low-latency profile that biases smaller batch windows and warmer KV cache policy.

[01:25] Samira: The unit cost goes up approx 30 to 50% depending on model family and seq len distribution, but p95 latency drops by about 20-35%. We've got the profiling spreadsheet linked.

[01:40] Elliot: Short question — are those numbers with prefix caching assumed? Because if customers implement passive prefix caching we get better economics.

[01:48] Samira: Yeah, the baseline assumes automatic KV cache with a 5 minute TTL. If customers can adopt explicit cache hints, the cost delta narrows. But, we can't always rely on client-side change.

[02:05] Noah: Also for Dedicated deployments we can change GPU tiling and kernel configs to reduce medians without massive cost — but that's infra-heavy and slow to roll.

[02:20] Liam: Right, the runtime can select lower-latency kernels at the expense of GPU utilization. It's doable, we've tested on a small cluster, but rollout risk is non-trivial.

[02:35] Maya: So tradeoffs are clear. How many customers would convert to the higher price if we offered a low-latency tier? Marcus?

[02:40] Marcus: Uh, from sales feedback, maybe 15-20% of current mid-market trials would pay a premium, especially fintech and media apps. Enterprise tends to want dedicated capacity or private anyway.

[02:55] Samira: My proposal: A) offer a named low-latency plan with documented price delta and recommend Dedicated for sustained needs; B) provide a short guide on caching patterns to shrink the gap.

[03:10] Rina: Also want to flag any regulatory constraints — in some APAC markets, the low-latency option may require data residency and we could get requests for private deployment.

[03:22] Maya: Good. Let's park that for the private deployment section. Next: headcount. Grace, how's hiring pulse?

[03:30] Grace: We're seeing candidate drop in a couple of IC roles — mostly due to comp comp vs market. I have a proposed Q1 cohort that prioritizes backend infra and SRE, two product managers, and three mid-level engineers for the runtime team. Total ask is 12 FTE and the cost is in the deck.

[03:50] Maya: The ask was a little higher than I expected. We need to align on tradeoffs — are these hires deferrable by a quarter?

[03:58] Grace: We could push two PMs, but infra and SRE hires are pretty time-sensitive given the Dedicated expansion.

[04:10] Maya: Okay. Finance wants a tighter top-down number. I'll take a draft off the table, but we won't approve until we reconcile with revenue trajectory. Expect me to push back on two roles.

[04:20] Elliot: On SRE — if we don't hire now, our oncall burden increases and MTTR could go up; that's a technical debt tax. The cost of not hiring could be higher if we have a Sev impacting customers.

[04:38] Liam: Agreed. We should probably surface a scenario analysis: cost of hire vs cost of potential downtime. I'll work with Grace on those numbers.

[04:50] Maya: Good. Next, private deployments — Noah you're up.

[04:55] Noah: Thanks. Slide 14 — pipeline and risk matrix. We currently have six active POCs for private (VPC and on-prem) and three legal security questionnaires in the queue. The big asks are KMS integration, SOC2 audit evidence, and air-gapped installer for on-prem. Also customers asking about data residency in EU & Australia.

[05:20] Noah: The quick win is offering managed VPC with customer KMS support. The harder part—on prem air-gap—needs a packaging sprint and legal sign off. I propose a tabletop exercise with Legal and Security to walk through one representative on-prem scenario.

[05:40] Rina: Yes, we need to test our compliance claims end-to-end. I'll lead the tabletop but need infra representation and product to show the installer steps.

[05:50] Samira: We also need to be honest with customers on our delivery timelines. Some customers assume a 2-week on-prem install; reality is 6-8 weeks with current staffing.

[06:05] Maya: Alright schedule that tabletop for week of Dec 13. Noah to own the invite and pre-read.

[06:12] Noah: Will do.

[06:15] Maya: Ops and reliability — Elliot?

[06:17] Elliot: We're prepping an ops runbook and incident playbooks. The runbook covers our primary failure modes: kernel OOMs, model NVLink errors, and scheduler deadlocks. We have draft runbooks on Confluence but the oncall rotation is not fully defined. We're proposing a 2-week primary rotation for infra and a 24/7 escalation path with an SRE lead.

[06:38] Elliot: Also want to propose a game day to validate the runbook in January.

[06:44] Maya: I like the game day. Samira, product is okay with scheduled downtime windows?

[06:49] Samira: For non-customer-impacting tests we can coordinate, but we need to communicate to the customers on Dedicated.

[06:56] Marcus: Sales asks we minimize surprises during pilots — they'd rather see a clear maintenance calendar.

[07:05] Maya: Good. Next — leadership glimpses and org changes. I want to be transparent: Tomas is leaving at the end of the year; leadership will reassign responsibilities for the infra squad. We'll run a performance interview process internally for Sr infra lead. HR and Grace will manage the comms.

[07:25] Grace: We'll draft the comms after we finalize reporting lines. Quick ask — do we want a hiring freeze for managers during the holiday blackout?

[07:34] Maya: Short answer: no across-the-board freeze. We'll evaluate manager hires case-by-case but lean conservative.

[07:40] Liam: On a different note — kernel-level improvements we've benchmarked versus CloudGen APIs look promising. If we ship the micro-optimizations in Q1 we should reclaim 10-12% token cost on average. Caveat: micro-opts increase CI surface and test flakiness.

[07:58] Samira: That's worth it. Add the micro-opts to the Q1 roadmap but guardrail with an automatic rollback policy.

[08:09] Maya: Okay, let's confirm: micro-opts go to canary in early Jan with rollback. Elliot you own the rollback instrumentation?

[08:16] Elliot: Yes. I'll put together the instrumentation checklist.

[08:20] [08:20] Rina: Legal closes — we need a single source of truth for customer contractual exceptions. Marcus, please funnel the exceptions into Legal's tracker so we can keep consistent precedence.

[08:30] Marcus: Will do.

[08:33] [08:33] Maya: Alright, quick recap and decisions: 1) Hold on full hiring approval until tighter budget alignment; Maya will circulate a revised deck. 2) Run private deployment tabletop week of Dec 13; Noah to coordinate. 3) Ops runbook + game day in Jan; Elliot to produce runbook by Dec 16. 4) Micro-optimization canary in Jan with rollback instrumentation. 5) Grace to send pulse survey. Any objections?

[08:58] Liam: No objections.

[09:02] Samira: None from product.

[09:05] Maya: Great. Final housekeeping: Marcus — please send to sales folks the language on low-latency tier and price delta, and Samira link the caching best practices doc.

[09:16] Marcus: Yep, I'll drop a short note in #go-to-market and attach the pricing schedule.

[09:22] Samira: I'll post the caching how-to and the profiling spreadsheet.

[09:28] Maya: Okay, thanks all. We'll meet next week for a short follow-up once Maya's deck is updated. Ending now.

[09:40] (recording end)

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription corrected some product names (XLA -> ex-el-la in raw), "KV cache" appears as "K V cash" or "K V cache" in portions. Speaker labels are mostly correct but a few brief overlaps show as separate lines.

Explicit next steps referenced in meeting: see action items above and the shared drive deck (https://drive.redwood/winter-deck-v3.pdf).

End of transcript.
